== Title ==
<span lang="ja">タンティヴィIV</span>. One asterisk precedes the printed title.<ref name="encyclopedia-172-full-source" />

== Card Text ==
<span lang="ja">パイロットを3人と、乗客を4人追加できる。ドッキング能力を持つ。能力値2の専属パイロットが搭乗している。どんな星系にでも配備できる（たとえ人員とフォース・アイコンがなくても）。</span><ref name="encyclopedia-172-full-source" />

== Lore ==
<span lang="ja">オルデラン総督家の外交船。レイア姫が帝国元老員としての職務（そして反乱軍の極秘任務）に使用した。タトゥイーン軌道上でデバステーターに拿捕された。</span><ref name="encyclopedia-172-full-source" />

== Translation of Japanese Text ==
AI English reading aid (Memory Core ChatGPT, 7 November 2026).

'''Title'''
<blockquote>Tantive IV</blockquote>

'''Lore'''
<blockquote>Diplomatic ship of the House of the Governor of Alderaan. Princess Leia used it for her duties as an Imperial senator (and for the Rebel Alliance's top-secret missions). Captured by the Devastator in orbit over Tatooine.</blockquote>

'''Game text'''
<blockquote>May add 3 pilots and 4 passengers. Has docking capability. A permanent pilot with ability 2 is aboard. May be deployed to any system (even without personnel and Force icons).</blockquote>

Both originals identify the ship as a capital corvette. The Japanese lore calls it a ship of the governor's house on Alderaan (総督家), where the English says "Royal House of Alderaan consular ship." The Japanese describes Leia's duties as an Imperial senator and the Rebels' secret missions, where the English says "Imperial Senate business" and "secret Rebel espionage." Both original game texts finish with deployment to any system. The Japanese parenthesis uses 人員とフォース・アイコン ("personnel and Force icons"), while the English says "presence or Force icons."<ref name="encyclopedia-172-full-source" /><ref name="english-face">[http://decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/anewhope/light/images/tantiveiv.gif Original English Tantive IV card face], [[Decipher]]. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20021025091946im_/http://decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/anewhope/light/images/tantiveiv.gif Internet Archive].</ref>

== Rules ==
The November 1998 [[Media:Decipher Glossary 1998.pdf|Decipher Glossary Version 2.0]] states that English is the standard for tournament play, directing foreign-language cards and rules to be played and interpreted as their English counterparts under current rulings, errata and clarifications.<ref name="foreign-language-rule">[[Media:Decipher Glossary 1998.pdf|Decipher Glossary Version 2.0]] (November 1998), p. 62, Foreign-language cards and rules.</ref>
